To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
proteins are good chiral selectors in liquid chromatography.

the enantioseparation of compounds on HPLC chiroselective stationary phases based on various proteins depends on a variety of factors such as protein structure, protein conformation, protein concentration and pH of the mobile phase.

the chiral recognition of various compounds using protein-based chiral stationary phase in HPLC is based on the interaction of the chiral compounds with the amino acid residues, especially the aromatic amino acid residues, of the protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: the preparation of HPLC stationary phases based on various proteins; the enantioseparation of different kinds of compounds; the enantiomeric separation mechanism; the effect of various experimental conditions on the enantio-separations; the application of these stationary phases in the enantioanalysis; and the development of new stationary phases based on protein engineering.
the enantioseparation of a large number of compounds on protein-based chiral stationary phase.
the use of proteins as the chirality source in the enantioseparation of compounds in HPLC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of proteins as chiral selectors in HPLC enantioseparation is a promising and useful approach for the enantiomeric separation of chiral compounds.
the use of proteins as chiral stationary phases in enantioselectivity-based HPLC is a promising and developing area.
the enantioseparation of various compounds using the proteins mentioned above as the chiral selector in HPLC has been demonstrated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the enantioseparation mechanism of the protein-based stationary phases involves the combination of hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic interactions, and electrostatic interactions, and the chiral recognition mechanism is mainly based on hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions.
the chiral recognition mechanisms for the enantioseparation of various compounds on the protein-based chiral stationary phase are complex and not well understood at the molecular level.
proteins are very versatile chiral selectors for enantioseparation of a wide range of chiral compounds in high-performance liquid chomatography (HPL C).
The main takeaway from our work is that
proteins are excellent chiral selectors for enantioseparation of various compounds in HPLC.
the enantioseparation of a wide range of compounds is possible using protein-based stationary phases.
the use of protein-based stationary phases in HPLC is a viable approach for the enantioseparation of chiral compounds.
